entries.name: Ìrántí

identity.nsec_path: N/A -- independently generated, not a BIPON39-derived sibling
identity.notes: Unlike Omo-Koda2/OpenClaw, Ìrántí is not reconciling a foreign identity root against minipae's derivation -- crates/iranti-core/src/store.rs::birth() calls nostr::Keys::generate() directly, minting a fresh native secp256k1/Nostr keypair as the agent's ONE identity, same shape as genteam-daemon/hermes's independent-nsec1 pattern already in this registry. No root-sharing question applies.

verified.notes: Stronger baseline than most entries here: Ìrántí IS a first-class NIP-AE producer/consumer natively (crypto.rs defines KIND_AGENT_ENGRAM=30174 plus companion kinds 36000-36003; bridge.rs's push()/pull() build and verify real signed kind:30174 events against any relay, unit-tested). This is source-confirmed, not yet re-run live against a public relay this session the way the omokoda/vantage bridge was -- engram_roundtrip reflects the existing tested code path, not a fresh live run; health:false until that live run happens.

identity.notes: sibling derivation from the same BIPON39 mnemonic every agent gets at birth (not a second unrelated key) -- resolves the root-sharing blocker this entry was waiting on. agent_index = minipae_index_for(agent_name) (first 4 bytes of sha256(name), masked to 31 bits); owner_index=0 (self-owned) until a real owner reconciliation policy exists. See omokoda-core/src/identity/wallet.rs::derive_minipae_key, wired into Steward::birth().

verified.notes: 2026-08-22 live e2e (two runs): built the real omokoda-cli binary, birthed a sovereign agent through Steward::dispatch(Statement::Birth) (real minipae_private_key_hex/minipae_npub derived and sealed), confirmed a real GlyphNode via a live `omokoda serve` instance's GET /v1/vault/glyph, then ran the real omokoda_adapter.py against a live kernel + a real public relay. Run 1: wss://relay.damus.io's query path returned HTTP 503 (known flakiness, matches prior session notes) -- push+pull both succeeded against wss://relay.primal.net instead. Run 2 (re-verified once damus.io recovered): push+pull both succeeded directly against wss://relay.damus.io -- `push` published 1/1 glyph nodes as NIP-AE engrams, `pull` round-tripped it back through the real POST /v1/vault/glyph/merge, independently re-confirmed via curl against the live server both times (node present, no duplication). Test agents + owner pointer cleaned up afterward each run; local default endpoint corrected to :8787 -> the real serve default port is configurable (tested against :8788).

entries.name: Triune Memory

identity.notes: Real, tested NIP-AE wire code already exists (src/nostr-wire.ts, via organism-core/bridge/nostr-wire, the canonical TypeScript wire implementation) and builds valid unsigned kind:30174 engrams -- but it holds no agent key by design (organism-core's TS module is one of the 'no-sign' implementations per this repo's own NAMESPACES.md) and is not yet called from orchestrator.ts/cli.ts/adapters.ts, so nothing publishes today. Open identity question, same shape as the OpenClaw entry above: Triune-Memory mirrors an existing Omo-Koda2 agentId 1:1 via SSE subscription (docs/OSO_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md) -- should it sign under that SAME agent's already-derived minipae key (Omo-Koda2's sealed vault would have to hand out a signature or a scoped delegation, not the raw key), or get its own sibling BIPON39-derived key as a distinct producer? Not decided -- surfaced, not silently bridged, matching the Iranti/Vantage-vault and Bondhive standalone-with-gate precedents.

entries.adapter: src/nostr-wire.ts (builds unsigned engrams only; no publish path wired yet)

verified.notes: 2026-08-22: confirmed real via source read -- buildEngram/buildSlug/KIND_AGENT_ENGRAM exist and are unit-tested (test/nostr-wire.test.mjs), but no caller in the orchestrator pipeline and no signer, so mem/triune/* has never had a real engram on the wire. Blocked on the identity decision above, not on missing code.

identity.notes: G4 (docs/RUNTIME_REGISTRY.md): OpenClaw has its own sovereign Ed25519 (BIPON39-derived) identity, not yet reconciled with the NIP-AE derivation path. Undecided whether that Ed25519 key IS the agent key (map into derivation) or stays runtime-local (separate nsec1). Stays 'planned' until decided - matches the BIPON39/NIP-06 sibling-derivation pattern already proven on Omo-Koda2's kernel, but no one has done the OpenClaw-side equivalent yet.

Vantage's OWN Buzz integration (buzz_identity.py, buzz_bridge.py in /opt/ares/Vantage/backend and ~/vantage-instance2/backend) already gives agents a sealed-seed Nostr identity - separate from and not yet reconciled with minipae's NIP-AE derivation. G2: stays planned until a real minipae adapter exists; the Buzz identity alone does not satisfy the bus contract (engram namespace).
